evals.prompt: Run a traceability review of the agonara intent layer (intent×intent — cross-role and inside-role slices).
evals.expected_output: A single Markdown findings file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ that reports the intent layer as clean (0 cross-role and 0 inside-role findings), backs that verdict with cited interlocking evidence, enumerates every story per file, and logs exactly the two known tensions as routed open questions rather than findings.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by the intent layer-pair (e.g. 2026-06-03T1007Z-intent.md).
The file front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the intent×intent layer-pair and the agonara project, and slices [cross-role, inside-role].

The front-matter inputs list the four intent-layer files (intent_learning_program_app.md, admin_user_stories.md, curator_user_stories.md, student_user_stories.md) each with its document version read from that file's own front-matter.
The Summary reports 0 cross-role findings and 0 inside-role findings (a clean verdict).

The clean verdict is supported by positive evidence: the cross-role section cites the interlocking corpus/student-state and membership-authority boundary passages with file:line, rather than merely asserting cleanliness.
The Inspected section enumerates all story IDs per file: INT-01 through INT-07, ADM-01 through ADM-15, CUR-01 through CUR-18, and STU-01 through STU-23.

An open question records the curator membership operation-vs-policy tension (CUR-14/CUR-17 perform invite/remove while the curator boundary disclaims defining membership policy) and routes it to a downstream layer (intent→ADR, e.g. ADR-006) instead of reporting it as a finding.
An open question records the self-join vs invitation join-mode taxonomy ambiguity (STU-18 vs STU-22), noting the product intent itself already flags it as open, instead of reporting it as a finding.
The reviewer reads only the four intent-layer files and does not read ADRs, specs, implementation plans, code, or tests.
The reviewer makes no edits to any source document, opens no PR, and creates no file other than the single findings file.
No false-positive findings are manufactured — in particular the Russian/English language difference between the product intent and the story bodies is not reported as a contradiction.

evals.prompt: Run a traceability review of the agonara intent → ADR layer-pair (fidelity and vertical coverage).
evals.expected_output: A findings file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ reporting the 16 ADRs as faithful to intent (0 contradictions) with two unacknowledged-loss warnings and one uncovered-capability warning, a full coverage matrix, and explicitly-deferred intent capabilities correctly excluded from findings.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by the intent-adr layer-pair (e.g. 2026-06-03T1050Z-intent-adr.md).

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the intent → ADR layer-pair and agonara, slices including fidelity and vertical-coverage, and an inputs list giving the four intent files with their versions and all 16 ADRs with their status.
The Inspected section confirms all 16 ADRs (adr-001 through adr-016) and all four intent files were read in full.
The Summary reports 0 fidelity fails, 2 fidelity warnings, 1 coverage warning, and 3 open questions.

The faithful core is backed by positive evidence cited into specific ADRs with file:line — at minimum the corpus/student-state separation, the LLM-not-accepted-until-curator boundary, Admin-is-not-a-learning-role, and the ownership statements.

A fidelity finding (warning, loss) records that the INT-02/STU-07 confusing-neighbor / concept-distinction commitment is narrowed away by ADR-010's closed accepted-corpus content list, quoting both the intent passage and the ADR-010 passage with file:line.

A fidelity finding (warning) records that CUR-13 pre-acceptance suggestion-origin visibility is carried by no ADR (ADR-010 carries only acceptance-time provenance), with the residual ambiguity routed to an open question rather than asserted as a hard contradiction.
A coverage finding (warning) records that CUR-09 coverage-gap discovery is carried by no ADR and not explicitly deferred (ADR-010 names gap analysis only as owned draft state).

Explicitly-deferred intent capabilities are classified as deferred and NOT reported as findings — in particular INT-06 period-level checks (ADR-016 names them a future slice), INT-07 interpretation, and STU-04/STU-05 session continuity.
A coverage matrix maps intent groups (by module) to the carrying ADR(s) with an explicit status of covered, deferred, or UNCOVERED.

All three open questions are tagged with a downstream resolving layer (ADR→spec), and no false-positive findings are made (an ADR deciding implementation detail the intent left open, or an explicit deferral, is not flagged).
